- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or increase early correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize it; add a “reversion buffer” to forecast: if price > 20% above recent high, cap forecast at 10–15% below that peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average sentiment over 3–5 periods to adjust forecast direction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trends; apply “look-back decay”: reduce weight of last 3–5 days in forecast if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
